finding: Both new emit sites (`ValidationError::at(e.layer(), e.code(), e.message(p), &s.id)` at 1273 and 1284) break this module's own finding drift-guard. `scan_ctor_call` (validate.rs:3114-3144) requires args 0 and 1 of `ValidationError::{err,at,warn}` to be PLAIN STRING LITERALS and pushes `scan.problems` otherwise ('the 1st argument … is not a string literal, so the drift guard cannot tell which layer/code it emits'); `validation_codes_are_registered_and_humanised` (3765) asserts `scan.problems.is_empty()`. So the backend unit suite fails as written. Worse structurally: with the old literal sites deleted, WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_{MISSING,UNSAFE,ESCAPE} are no longer in the scanner's `emitted` set at all, so the `stale` assertion (3796) also fires AND — if the guard is later 'fixed' by relaxing it — those three codes silently lose both the VALIDATION_CODES registry check and the validationCopy.ts HUMAN_COPY check. Every other emit site in the file keeps the literal shape (641/648/661/672/683/706/712/727/…): this is the only pair that deviates. Fix: keep the constructor literal-shaped (`match e { Unsafe => at("security","WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE", e.message(p), &s.id), … }`) or teach `scan_ctor_call` about the accessor form.

Dependency direction is inverted. `read_prompt_file` puts RUNTIME behaviour — canonicalize + `std::fs::read_to_string` returning the full prompt body — inside the VALIDATOR, and `dispatch.rs:136` (the runner) now reaches into `crate::modules::workflow::validate` to execute it. The validator is a pure verdict producer everywhere else in this module; the runner already has a file-IO owner (`file_io.rs`) and `dispatch.rs` previously used `tokio::fs` directly. The shared rule should live in a neutral leaf (e.g. `workflow/prompt.rs`) that BOTH `validate.rs` and `dispatch.rs` depend on, with validate.rs mapping the neutral error onto findings. As written, 'runtime reads its prompt through the validator' is a coupling that will be copied by the next shared rule.

`PromptFileError` mixes the CAUSE with the validator's PRESENTATION. `code()` (a wire finding code the builder keys copy off) and `layer()` (the stringly-typed "semantic"/"security" bucket) are meaningful only to `check_prompt_files`, yet they are `pub` on the type the RUNNER imports — `dispatch.rs` gets both in scope and must know not to use them. `message()` is documented as 'Author-facing detail', so the runner's operator-visible step error (dispatch.rs:142) is now authored by the builder's copy vocabulary: a wording change made for the validation panel silently rewrites text persisted into `workflow_runs`. Separating the cause enum (Unsafe/Escape/Unreadable/Empty) from a validator-side `fn finding(&self, rel, step) -> ValidationError` would leave the runner depending only on the cause — and would also restore the literal call shape the drift guard needs (see the high finding).

Two doc comments added by this same diff contradict each other on the load-bearing claim. `read_prompt_file`'s doc (1203-1206) says the TOCTOU window is safe because the bundle is 'server-owned and re-validated immediately before dispatch'; `load_raw_prompt`'s doc (dispatch.rs:119-121) says the opposite — 'The runner does not get to rely on having been validated: `POST /workflows/{id}/test` reaches dispatch without `validate_for_install`' — which is the entire justification for duplicating the check in the runner. One of the two is wrong, and the wrong one is the security rationale.

The claimed de-duplication is only half done: `PromptSource::Missing`/`Both` re-author the sentences the validator already owns ('has neither prompt: nor prompt_file:' at validate.rs:715, 'has both prompt: and prompt_file: (mutually exclusive)' at validate.rs:709) as separate `format!`s here, with no guard tying them together — while the FILE branch (line 142) correctly reuses `e.message(rel)`. So the same message text exists in two places for two of the four outcomes, and the treatment is asymmetric within one `match`. TEST-6 pins the dispatch strings by exact equality but nothing pins them to the validator's, so they can drift apart silently.

`prompt_source(prompt: &Option<String>, prompt_file: &Option<String>)` — the two parameters are adjacent, identically typed, and semantically opposite. `prompt_source(f, p)` compiles and silently inverts the rule: an inline prompt body becomes `PromptSource::File(<the prompt text>)`, which the runner then tries to open as a bundle-relative path. `load_raw_prompt(step_id, bundle_root, prompt, prompt_file)` (dispatch.rs:122) repeats the hazard, and `step_id: &str` is now first with no type distinction from any other `&str`. Since the canonical producer is already `StepConfig::prompt_fields()`, the misuse-proof signature is `prompt_source(cfg: &StepConfig) -> Option<PromptSource<'_>>` (or a `PromptFields` newtype), which also removes the tuple-order knowledge from every call site.

`promptField`'s doc (189-193) now claims it 'MIRRORS `validate.rs::prompt_source` … inline = prompt.filter(|s| !s.is_empty())', but the non-file branch is `z.string().trim().min(1, required)` — it TRIMS. `prompt: "   "` is `PromptSource::Inline("   ")` (valid) to the backend and 'A prompt is required' (red) in the builder; DEC-3 deliberately chose is_empty() in Rust precisely to avoid changing that. The new Rust drift guard `client_prompt_file_predicate_mirrors_prompt_source` only inspects `promptSuppliedByFile`, i.e. the prompt_FILE half, so the inline half is both divergent and unguarded — the exact 'two places decide separately' shape the change claims to have closed, one field over.

Stale comment describing code this diff deleted — in three files: LlmStepForm.tsx:31-36, LlmMapStepForm.tsx:61-65, AgentStepForm.tsx:71-75 all still say 'dispatch.rs's load_raw_prompt, which matches only (Some,None)/(None,Some), fails the RUN with "invalid prompt config"'. `load_raw_prompt` no longer matches `(Option, Option)` and the string 'invalid prompt config' no longer exists anywhere. They also cite `has_prompt`, a local that was renamed to `inline` inside `prompt_source`. These comments are the justification for the `prompt: v || null` normalisation, so a future reader will conclude the normalisation is now unnecessary.

The new `StepConfig::prompt_fields()` seam is not adopted where the same 'which kinds are model-backed' question is asked with a CLOSED, silent construct: runner.rs:1262 and runner.rs:1563 use `matches!(s.config, Llm{..}|LlmMap{..}|Agent{..})` to decide `require_model`, and test_runner.rs:111 uses the same shape for mock coverage. Adding a new prompt-carrying kind is a compile error in `prompt_fields()` (good) but SILENT in all three `matches!` sites — and the failure mode is a panic, since runner.rs:773/779/787 `.expect("llm step requires a resolved model + provider")` after `require_model` came back false. Route these through `prompt_fields().is_some()` (or a `StepConfig::needs_model()` sibling) so the seam actually covers the class.

Adding a new prompt-rejection reason: a new `PromptFileError` variant forces edits to `code()`, `layer()` and `message()` (three compile errors — good), but `code()` invites reusing an existing code, and `Unreadable(_) | Empty => "WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING"` already collapses two distinct causes onto one wire code. That collapse is why validationCopy.ts:110 had to become a four-way disjunction ('missing, be a folder, be empty, or not be text') instead of the targeted remedy the backend actually knows. A fifth cause folded into MISSING would make that sentence quietly incomplete with NO test failing — and, per the high finding, the HUMAN_COPY guard no longer reaches these codes at all. Either give each cause its own code, or surface the cause as a structured field the copy can switch on.

`read_prompt_file` returns the whole file body to a caller that discards it: `check_prompt_files` (1283) does `if let Err(e) = read_prompt_file(...)`, so every install/import validation now fully reads every prompt file into a String purely to test emptiness — with no size cap anywhere, and synchronously (`std::fs::read_to_string`) on the async handler thread (`validate_collecting` is called directly from `handlers/dev.rs:107` and the install path). The doc's justification ('Reading the file IS the check … no weaker proxy can drift from it') is sound for the RUNNER, but the validator only needs the verdict; a `read_prompt_file` + `check_prompt_file(…) -> Result<(), PromptFileError>` pair (the latter discarding the body, both sharing one impl) keeps the anti-drift property without making validation an unbounded read.

Stale symbol citation in the changed region: 'UNSAFE (`validate.rs::check_prompt_files`, the literal `..` / leading-`/` reject)'. That reject moved out of `check_prompt_files` into the new `check_prompt_file_shape` (validate.rs:1179) in this same diff; `check_prompt_files` no longer contains the literal test. Line-number citations broken by this diff and not updated: gallery.tsx:439 and :496 cite 'validate.rs:684' for WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING (now emitted at validate.rs:713) and :445/:503 cite 'validate.rs:729' for WORKFLOW_TOOL_NO_TOOL (now 760). The fixture's whole documented value is that each quadruple is 'copied from the emit site named beside it', so the pointers are load-bearing. Cite the function name rather than a line.

New `pub` surface with no consumer outside validate.rs: `prompt_file_ref` (1121, called only at 1267 and inside `prompt_source`), `check_prompt_file_shape` (1179, called only at 1272 and inside `read_prompt_file`), and `PromptFileError::code`/`layer` (1643/1652, called only at 1273/1284). Only `prompt_source`, `PromptSource`, `read_prompt_file` and `PromptFileError::message` are actually cross-module. CODING_GUIDELINES §15 treats `pub` with no external consumer as unfinished wiring (and the `pub` also suppresses dead-code detection). Make the in-module-only ones `pub(crate)`/private.

`check_prompt_files` calls `check_prompt_file_shape(p)` at 1272 and then `read_prompt_file(bundle_root, p)` at 1283, which re-runs `check_prompt_file_shape(rel)` at 1208. Harmless today (both paths produce the same finding) but it means the shape check has two live entry points in one loop, and the `continue` at 1274 is the only thing preventing a duplicate finding. A comment saying why the double call is deliberate — or hoisting shape out of `read_prompt_file` and documenting that the runner must call both — would stop the next reader 'simplifying' one away.

The new 20-line comment claims the OLD values were bad partly because they 'were also off the 4px spacing scale', then describes the replacement as 'Grid-aligned logical padding instead: 8px bare, 4px beside a button, 6px beside a kbd' — but 6px (`ps-1.5`/`pe-1.5`, lines 53/55) is itself a 2px half-step, not on the 4px grid. The stated rationale therefore does not support the code as written (the half-step may be fine — DESIGN_SYSTEM notes the kit uses them — but then the criticism of the old values should not rest on grid alignment). The measured figures ('3.20px -> 4.00px', '5.61px -> 6.00px') are also snapshot values with no test pinning them, inside a `cva` variants object where they will rot unnoticed.

`REVERTED_RULE` is documented as 'The exact rule that was removed' and the control test says it 're-injects the EXACT rule that was removed — conditional on a `> button` child, exactly as the kit had it'. It injects `margin-inline-end:-0.3rem`; what was removed was `mr-[-0.3rem]`, i.e. the PHYSICAL `margin-right`. Equivalent in the LTR-only control, but the whole point of the fix was physical→logical, so the control silently proves the probe catches a LOGICAL revert while the regression it guards against would be a physical one. Either inject `margin-right` (matching history) or drop the word EXACT.

`PromptFileError::message(&self, rel: &str)` makes the caller re-supply the path the error is about — two call sites (validate.rs:1273/1284 pass `p`, dispatch.rs:142 passes `rel`) each of which could pass the canonicalized path, another step's path, or nothing meaningful, with no compile-time link. Capturing `rel` in the variant at construction (or returning the message from `read_prompt_file`'s Err) removes the hazard. Related inconsistency: the runner's Missing/Both errors are prefixed `step '{step_id}'` while its file errors (via `message`) carry no step id at all, so a multi-step run reports 'prompt_file ... is empty' with nothing identifying the step.

The constant is now documented as 'pure sub-pixel jitter slack, with NO defect allowance', but it is still named `MAX_TOLERATED_OVERFLOW_PX` — a name that reads as a defect budget and was the reason it could quietly sit at 4. The new spec expresses the same concept as `JITTER_PX` (input-group-overflow.spec.ts:41) with the correct name, so the two files now carry one concept under two names. Rename here to match.

`prompt_fields()`'s doc overclaims history: 'Every site that needs this pair used to write its own open `if let`/`match` with a silent fallthrough (`_ => None`, `_ => (None, None)`) … quietly skipped by the validator and the runner alike.' The `_ => None` site existed (old `check_prompt_files`); no `_ => (None, None)` site is in the diff or the tree, and the RUNNER never had a pair-with-fallthrough site — its three dispatchers destructure their own kind with `_ => return Failed`. Today `prompt_fields()` still has no runner caller (dispatch.rs uses it only in a test at :2050), so 'the runner alike' describes a coupling the code does not have.

The `PROMPT_CODES` guard derives its expected set from `include_str!("validate.rs")` scanning for `"WORKFLOW_PROMPT`. Two consequences worth a comment: (a) it matches ANY such literal, including the ones in validate.rs's own `#[cfg(test)]` assertions and in `VALIDATION_CODES`, so a test that merely mentions a hypothetical code fails the guard; (b) it scans only validate.rs, so a prompt verdict emitted from `ref_check.rs` (which also builds ValidationErrors) would be invisible. Contrast the sibling guard 20 lines away, whose doc insists on RUNTIME reads 'never `include_str!`, which would freeze a stale snapshot' — the inconsistency is defensible for same-crate Rust but is not explained.

On the TS side, 'which kinds carry a prompt' is encoded a third time as the hand-maintained `PROMPT_XOR_KINDS` list (and a fourth time as the per-case `promptField(...)` calls in `buildStepZodSchema`, stepForms.ts:274/282/289). A new prompt-carrying kind is a compile error in Rust's `prompt_fields()` but is SILENTLY uncovered by both new TS tests, which iterate that literal list. Deriving it from `STEP_KINDS` filtered by a single exported predicate would make the TS side fail loudly the same way.

REJECTED: `dispatch.rs` importing from `validate.rs` is not itself new coupling — `validate.rs` already owns `StepDef`/`StepConfig`/`OnError`/`OutputFormat` and dispatch.rs already imported them before this diff. The direction problem is specifically the runtime FILE READ moving into the validator (see the separate finding), not the import edge.

REJECTED: wrapping the sync `read_prompt_file` in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` does not violate CODING_GUIDELINES §5 'no std::fs in async' — the blocking pool is the sanctioned escape hatch and the comment states the reason. (The blocking-in-async problem is on the VALIDATOR side, which calls `std::fs::read_to_string` straight from an async handler; that is filed separately.)

REJECTED: `rel.contains("..")` over-rejects legitimate filenames such as `notes..md` and misses Windows-shaped absolutes (`C:\`). Both are pre-existing and unchanged by this diff, the doc explicitly calls it the 'literal' textual reject, and the canonicalize+`starts_with(root)` confinement below catches the Windows case as Escape rather than Unsafe.

REJECTED: canonicalizing before the confinement test means a BROKEN symlink pointing outside the bundle reports `Unreadable` → WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING rather than ESCAPE. Ordering is pre-existing, both outcomes are install-blocking errors, and the run refuses either way — INV-1 holds.

REJECTED: editing a file under `sdk/packages/kit/src/shadcn/` looks like the DESIGN_SYSTEM 'never edit shadcn/ or kit/ to restyle app UI' violation, but that rule targets app-level restyling; here the kit component IS the defect owner and the fix is a containment bug, not a restyle. Fixing it at the source (and deleting the downstream tolerance constant) is the correct direction.

REJECTED: TEST-1's hardcoded `checked == 108` / `ran_ok == 18` look like magic numbers that will rot. Verified consistent with the matrix as written (3 kinds x 4 prompts x 9 files = 108; per kind the runnable rows are {absent,""}x real.md plus {"   ","hi"}x{absent,""} = 6, x3 = 18) and both are anti-vacuity guards that SHOULD fail loudly when the input arrays change.

REJECTED: `PromptSource<'a>` borrowing `&'a str` out of the caller's `Option<String>`s is a lifetime hazard. The lifetime is tied to the inputs and both call sites consume it immediately; making it owned would only add allocations on the hot dispatch path.

REJECTED: adding the bare path `sdk` to the pull_request paths filter looks like it would not match a submodule change. A gitlink bump is a change to the tree entry at path `sdk`, so GitHub's path filter does match it; the added comment states the rationale correctly.
